en.title: Unordered Pairs Satisfying an Absolute Value Condition
en.description:
Given an integer array and sumVal, an unordered pair (i,j) of distinct indices is called an interesting pair when |arr[i]-arr[j]|+|arr[i]+arr[j]| equals sumVal. Count such pairs.

The standard input/output, the ranges added by this site, and the examples follow this problem's description; wherever the source's ranges are missing, they are explicitly marked as this site's additions.
en.input: The first line contains n and sumVal, and the second line contains n integers. This site's additions: 1≤n≤100000, −10^9≤arr[i]≤10^9, −2×10^9≤sumVal≤2×10^9; the result uses a 64-bit integer. The original snapshot did not provide these ranges.
en.output: Output the number of unordered index pairs that satisfy the condition.
en.explanation: Use the identity |x−y|+|x+y|=2·max(|x|,|y|). If sumVal is a non-negative even number, let r=sumVal/2; the answer is the number of element pairs whose absolute values are both at most r, minus the number of pairs whose absolute values are both less than r.
hints: Use the identity |x−y|+|x+y|=2·max(|x|,|y|). If sumVal is a non-negative even number, let r=sumVal/2; the answer is the number of element pairs whose absolute values are both at most r, minus the number of pairs whose absolute values are both less than r.
